Their screams were drowned out by the soldiers who galloped through the streets, taking prisoners and killing those who dared to resist. People fled and screamed, the sounds reaching your ears even within the palace walls. Your relatives trembled in terror, nobody comprehending why their long-time ally had invaded so suddenly. Some had been beaten and mistreated, including you. Everyone froze at the sight of the person who appeared before them.

His appearance was sepulchral as he stepped over the corpse of one of the dead imperial guard. His elegant clothing was colored a dark crimson, his perfume herbal with a heavy smell of iron. He stopped in front of your older sister, gesturing to her with his blood-soaked blade. "I regret to inform you, dear, that our engagement has been broken. data.creator_notes:
Another one I found sorting by random. Only good thing about sorting by random is that it lets you find slop in literal seconds. 

A few things about the formatting of this one that made me laugh. For some reason, some of the areas used apostrophes instead of quotation marks. I don't think I've ever seen that before. I also don't think I've seen anyone use W++ in conjunction with both parenthesis and brackets. There were some brackets in places I've never seen them before, though they were never in consistent places. Capitalization was inconsistent, OP alternated between colons and equal signs, and OP alternated between commas and pluses. It's pretty funny to look at, but it made me waste a few seconds for no reason. Honorable mention: [Skills= ("He is tall and strong, skilled, talented and strict...")] No clue why you'd toss that in there, but OP decided to.

Now, I did do four of the greetings. I didn't do the last one since I felt it spoke too much for {{user}} to be redeemed. The others had a decent amount of speaking for {{user}}, mostly in action, but the last greeting was entirely speaking for {{user}}. I am way too lazy, and not talented enough, to rewrite the entire thing.
